title: Ethiopian Bird's Eye Chilli Powder
community: All of Ethiopia — the fierce finishing spice
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Mitmita — a very fine, orange-red powder of bird's eye chillies, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. Ethiopia's finishing spice — used on kitfo, gored gored, eggs, and anywhere a quick hit of intense heat and fragrance is needed.
longDesc: Mitmita is the finishing spice of Ethiopian cooking — fiercely hot from bird's eye chillies but fragrant from cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon. It is sprinkled on kitfo and gored gored, stirred into kibbeh, and used wherever a powerful finishing spice is needed. Finer and more aromatic than berbere.
steps: Toast bird's eye chillies briefly in a dry pan — 1—2 minutes.
Grind chillies to a very fine powder.
Add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and salt.
chefTips: Mitmita should be very finely ground — finer than berbere.
Very hot — use sparingly if not accustomed to intense heat.
The cardamom fragrance should be clearly present.
commonMistakes: Coarse grinding — too chunky for the finishing applications.
cookingScience: Bird's eye chillies contain 100,000—225,000 Scoville Heat Units of capsaicin — among the highest of commonly used dried chillies. The cardamom's 1,8-cineole and the cloves' eugenol are both aromatic volatile compounds that partially offset the pure heat perception by stimulating other receptors simultaneously.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian bird's eye chillies — locally grown.
healthBenefits: Very high capsaicin — thermogenic and anti-inflammatory.
culturalNote: Mitmita is Ethiopia's fiercest spice — the one that tests how much heat you can handle. The experienced Ethiopian eater uses it liberally on kitfo; the first-time visitor approaches it with caution. Its orange-red colour and intense fragrance are immediately distinctive.
